giCatalog.sourcePolicy: Fineli supplies available-carbohydrate quantities only. GI evidence is stored as individual, traceable records on the glucose scale. STRONG values must be published and ISO 26642-confirmed; they support direct food and preparation matches only. Published SUPPLEMENTARY values and explicitly sourced analogues may support a low-confidence ingredient estimate when food and preparation relevance are documented. CATEGORY_MEAN values are broad proxies, never described as measurements of the named food, and force LOW confidence. Study quality and food/preparation match quality remain separate. For a missing GI match on a positive portion below 1 g available carbohydrate per serving, omission is an editorial tolerance only when all such recipe portions sum to less than 2 g per serving; the omitted carbohydrate amount is disclosed. This is not a clinical error bound. Larger known carbohydrate portions require GI evidence. The formula is an ingredient-sum estimate, not a measurement of a prepared meal. Do not copy complete source tables or substitute unsupported foods/preparations.

source.qualityEvidence: Supplemental Table 1 entry 1861 identifies mashed potato, NS (China, test year 2005), GI 73 ± 3, n=10, a 50 g available-carbohydrate portion, glucose/2 h and standard timepoints. It lists venous samples but the assay method as NS. Yang et al. (2006; https://doi.org/10.3748/wjg.v12.i21.3430), the underlying primary study cited in the 2021 non-western compendium, independently reports a distinct mashed-potato row at 73.0 ± 9.2 (n=10) and a cooked-potato row at 66.4 ± 3.8. This confirms the products and values are distinct; Yang does not specify the cooking method for the cooked-potato row. Table membership supports the review's ISO-methodology classification, but the original assay details cannot be independently verified.

source.title: Glycemic indices, glycemic load and glycemic response for seventeen varieties of dates grown in Saudi Arabia
source.authors: AlGeffari MA, Almogbel ES, Alhomaidan HT, El-Mergawi R, Barrimah IA
source.table: Table 2; mean GI 55.2 (SEM 7.7), range 42.8–74.6 across 17 Tamer-stage varieties; glucose reference
source.qualityEvidence: Published human GI study in 19 healthy adults. Each Tamer-stage date variety was tested once in 9–10 participants using a 50 g available-carbohydrate portion and glucose reference. The reported across-variety mean was 55.2 (SEM 7.7), with a wide 42.8–74.6 range; variety differences were not statistically significant, but this is not ISO 26642-confirmed and does not establish values for other ripeness stages or cooked date mixtures.

records.note: Low-confidence food-family mean for unsweetened Tamer-stage dried dates as sold. Use only when the recipe names dried dates added without further cooking; do not apply to date paste, syrup, fresh/semi-ripe dates, or dates cooked into a dish. This ingredient estimate is not a measurement of the recipe or meal.

records.preparation: Steam-cooked and gelatinized with water and 5 g groundnut oil; India, 1991

source.title: Glycaemic index of conventional carbohydrate meals
source.authors: Mani UV, Pradhan SN, Mehta NC, Thakur DM, Iyer U, Mani I
source.table: International Tables 2021 Supplemental Table 2 item 2762 and Mani et al. 1992 Table 3 meal R1: GI 55 ± 9; semolina steamed and gelatinized with 5 g groundnut oil; type 2 diabetes, n=6; 50 g available-carbohydrate portion; glucose reference; 0/60/120 minute timepoints.
source.qualityEvidence: The 2021 international tables place this result in Supplemental Table 2 because of method deviations: only six participants with type 2 diabetes, no repeated reference, and 0/60/120 minute sampling. The measured preparation is steam-cooked and gelatinized with water plus 5 g groundnut oil. The cited source does not establish equivalence with this recipe’s water-boiled, oil-free porridge or isolate the effect of the added oil. Retain the record for the tested preparation; do not map it to water-boiled semolina porridge without supporting evidence.

records.note: GI 55 is retained for the source-tested steam-gelatinized semolina with groundnut oil. It is not an accepted GI match for water-boiled, oil-free semolina porridge; do not present it as a measurement of this recipe or its mixed meal.

source.table: Supplemental Table 1 item 1150: navel oranges, Australia, GI 45 ± 5; 10 healthy adults; 50 g available carbohydrate; glucose, 2 h; ISO-consistent standard method.
source.qualityEvidence: Published food-specific navel-orange measurement listed in Supplemental Table 1 as ISO 26642:2010-consistent. Source quality is strong; the recipe uses a generic raw peeled orange with unknown cultivar, so the recipe mapping remains a low-confidence analogue.

records.note: Direct source for raw navel orange; use for generic raw orange only as a cultivar analogue and retain LOW confidence when cultivar is unknown. Not a measurement of a recipe or meal.
